title: Moroccan Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemon
summary: Tender chicken braised with olives, preserved lemon and saffron in a fragrant onion sauce.
ingredients: 800 g chicken thigh, bone-in and skin-on
1 preserved lemon, flesh discarded, rind rinsed and cut into strips

stages.title: Season the chicken and prepare the aromatics
steps: Pat the chicken thighs dry with paper towel, then rub them with the salt, ginger and turmeric.
Thinly slice the onions and finely chop the garlic.
Quarter the preserved lemon, scrape out and discard the flesh, rinse the rind under cold water and cut it into thin strips.
Crumble the saffron into the chicken stock and leave it to infuse until needed.

stages.title: Brown the chicken and soften the onions
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large heavy-based pot or tagine over medium-high heat.
Cook the chicken skin-side down for 6–7 minutes until deep golden, then turn and cook for 2 minutes more. Lift onto a plate.
Reduce the heat to medium, add the onions to the same pot and cook for 8 minutes, stirring often, until soft and lightly golden.
Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.

stages.title: Simmer the tagine
steps: Pour in the saffron stock and scrape up the browned bits from the base of the pot.
Return the chicken to the pot with any juices, skin-side up, and bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Cover, reduce to low heat and cook for 20 minutes.
Add the preserved lemon rind and olives, cover again and cook for 10 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through with no pink near the bone and the juices run clear.

stages.title: Reduce the sauce and serve
steps: Uncover the pot and simmer over medium heat for 5 minutes until the sauce is glossy and slightly thickened.
Meanwhile, cook the couscous according to the packet.
Stir half the coriander through the tagine, then serve over the couscous scattered with the remaining coriander.

tips: Rinsing the preserved lemon rind removes excess salt, so the sauce tastes bright rather than harsh.
Skin-on, bone-in thighs stay juicy through the long simmer and add body to the sauce.
Browning the chicken well first builds a deeper flavour base than simmering it straight from raw.
Crumbling the saffron into warm stock draws out more colour and aroma than adding the threads dry.
variations: Swap the green olives for kalamata olives for a saltier, fruitier flavour.
Add 1 cup of drained chickpeas with the stock to make the dish more filling.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat gently in a covered pot over low heat until steaming hot, adding a splash of water if the sauce is thick.

title: Sichuan Mapo Tofu
summary: Silken tofu and minced pork simmered in a fiery, numbing chilli-bean sauce with Sichuan pepper.
ingredients: 500 g soft tofu, cut into 2 cm cubes
1 tbsp fermented black beans, roughly chopped

stages.title: Prepare the tofu and peppercorns
steps: Toast the Sichuan peppercorns in a dry wok over medium heat for 1–2 minutes, until fragrant. Tip into a mortar and crush coarsely, then set aside.
Bring 1 litre water to a gentle simmer in a saucepan over medium heat and stir in the salt.
Slide in the tofu cubes and simmer for 2 minutes, then drain gently in a sieve. Blanching firms the tofu so it holds its shape.
Mix the cornflour with 2 tbsp cold water in a small bowl until smooth, and set aside.

stages.title: Build the flavour base
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in the wok over medium-high heat. Add the pork mince and cook for 4–5 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and no longer pink.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the doubanjiang and fermented black beans and fry for 1 minute, until the oil turns red.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant.

stages.title: Simmer the tofu
steps: Pour in the chicken stock and bring to a simmer over medium heat, scraping up any bits stuck to the wok.
Add the tofu and gently push it into the sauce with the back of a spatula. Simmer for 5 minutes without stirring vigorously, so the tofu absorbs the flavours and stays whole.

stages.title: Thicken and serve
steps: Stir the cornflour mixture again, then pour in about half. Simmer for 1 minute, shaking the wok gently, until the sauce lightly coats the tofu. Add the rest if you want it thicker.
Scatter over the crushed peppercorns and spring onions.
Serve straight away with cooked rice, prepared according to the packet.

tips: Blanching the tofu in salted water firms it up and seasons it, so the cubes survive simmering without breaking.
Frying the doubanjiang in oil until it turns red releases its colour and deepens its savoury flavour; raw paste tastes harsh.
Toast and crush the Sichuan peppercorns just before serving, as their numbing aroma fades quickly once ground.
Push and fold the tofu with the back of a spatula instead of stirring, which breaks soft tofu apart.
variations: Replace the pork with 200 g finely chopped mushrooms, cooked for 6–8 minutes until golden, and use vegetable stock. Check the labels on the doubanjiang and black beans.
For a milder version, use 1 tbsp doubanjiang and add 1 tsp soy sauce for seasoning.
storage: Cool and refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat gently in a saucepan over low heat until steaming hot, adding a splash of water if needed. Tofu texture suffers when frozen, so freezing is not recommended.

title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
summary: Smoky grilled chicken with allspice, thyme, spring onion and Scotch bonnet heat, brightened with lime.
ingredients: 1 lime, cut into wedges, to serve

stages.title: Make the jerk marinade
steps: Wearing gloves, roughly chop the deseeded Scotch bonnet chilli.
Add the spring onions, garlic, chilli, allspice, dried thyme, soy sauce, lime juice, brown sugar and vegetable oil to a small blender or food processor.
Blend for 30–45 seconds into a rough, spoonable paste.

stages.title: Marinate the chicken
steps: Pat the drumsticks dry with paper towel and cut 2–3 deep slashes through the thickest part of each one.
Put the drumsticks in a large non-metallic dish and pour over the marinade.
Rub the marinade into the slashes and under the skin, then cover the dish.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, turning the drumsticks once halfway.

stages.title: Cook the chicken
steps: Take the chicken out of the fridge 20 minutes before cooking, and heat a barbecue with a lid to medium (about 180°C) set up for indirect cooking, or heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) with a rack over a lined tray.
Put the drumsticks on the indirect side of the barbecue (or on the rack in the oven), skin side up.

Cook with the lid closed, turning every 10 minutes, for 35 minutes, or until the skin is deeply browned and the meat is cooked through with no pink near the bone and clear juices (75°C on a thermometer).

stages.title: Char and rest
steps: Move the drumsticks over direct medium-high heat, or under a hot oven grill, for 3–5 minutes, turning often, until the skin is charred in spots but not burnt.
Rest the chicken on a plate for 5 minutes.
Serve the drumsticks with the lime wedges.

tips: Wear gloves and keep the seeds out of the Scotch bonnet, because the seeds and membrane hold most of the heat. Use half a chilli for a milder result.
Cooking over indirect heat first cooks the bone-in meat through before the sugar in the marinade has a chance to burn.
Slashing the drumsticks lets the marinade reach the meat, so the flavour goes deeper than the skin.
Resting the chicken keeps the juices in the meat instead of running out when you cut it.
variations: Use chicken thighs with the bone in, and cook for the same time, until the juices run clear.
Add 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon to the marinade for a warmer, sweeter spice note.
storage: Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat in a 180°C (160°C fan) oven for 15 minutes, or until steaming hot all the way through. Freeze for up to 2 months.

title: Turkish İmam Bayıldı
summary: Soft roasted aubergines filled with sweet onions, tomatoes and garlic, finished with fruity olive oil.

stages.title: Roast the eggplants
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Halve the eggplants lengthways, then cut 3 or 4 deep slits into each cut face without piercing the skin.
Brush the cut sides with 2 tbsp of the olive oil and sprinkle with half the salt.
Place cut-side up on a lined baking tray and roast for 25 minutes, until the flesh is golden and softened.

stages.title: Cook the filling
steps: While the eggplants roast, heat 2 tbsp of the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Cook the onions for 10 minutes, stirring often, until soft and lightly golden.
Add the garlic and tomato paste and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, sugar, the remaining salt and the pepper, then cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and jammy.
Stir in half the parsley and take the pan off the heat.

stages.title: Stuff and bake
steps: Press a hollow along each roasted eggplant half with a spoon, taking care not to break the skin.
Spoon the filling into the hollows, mounding it on top.
Pack the eggplants snugly in a baking dish, pour the 150 ml water around them and drizzle with the remaining 2 tbsp olive oil.
Cover tightly with foil and bake for 40 minutes, until the eggplant is very tender and collapsing when pressed.

stages.title: Rest and finish
steps: Rest the eggplants, covered, for 5 minutes.
Spoon the pan juices over the top, drizzle with the lemon juice and scatter with the remaining parsley.

tips: Deep slits let the oil and filling flavour reach the flesh, so the eggplant cooks through evenly.
Salting and roasting the eggplant first drives off moisture, which prevents a watery, bitter result.
Ripe tomatoes give the best filling; if yours are pale, the tomato paste adds depth.
Serve warm or at room temperature, as the flavours settle and improve as it cools.
variations: Add 2 tbsp toasted pine nuts and 2 tbsp currants to the filling for a sweeter, richer version.
Add 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon to the tomato mixture for a spiced finish.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 4 days and serve cold or at room temperature. Reheat gently in a 160°C (140°C fan) oven for 15 minutes if you prefer it warm.

title: French Chicken Chasseur
summary: Golden chicken braised with mushrooms, shallots, white wine and tomatoes in a glossy herb sauce.
ingredients: 8 chicken thigh cutlets, bone in, skin on (about 1 kg)

stages.title: Prepare and season
steps: Pat the chicken dry with paper towel so the skin browns rather than steams.
Season the chicken all over with the salt and black pepper.
Slice the mushrooms and finely chop the shallots and garlic.
Drain the canned diced tomatoes lightly if very watery, then measure out 200 g.
Chop the tarragon and set it aside.

stages.title: Brown the chicken
steps: Heat the olive oil and half the butter in a large deep frying pan or casserole over medium-high heat.
Cook the chicken skin-side down for 5–6 minutes, until deep golden.
Turn and brown the other side for 4 minutes, then transfer to a plate.
Pour off all but 1 tbsp of fat from the pan.

stages.title: Build the sauce
steps: Reduce the heat to medium and add the remaining butter. Cook the mushrooms for 6–7 minutes, until their liquid has evaporated and they are browned.
Add the shallots and garlic and cook for 2–3 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and flour and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the white wine, scraping up the browned bits, and simmer for 3–4 minutes until reduced by half.

stages.title: Simmer and finish
steps: Add the chicken stock and the canned diced tomatoes and bring to a simmer over medium heat, about 3 minutes.
Return the chicken to the pan, skin-side up, with any juices from the plate.
Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Remove the lid and simmer for 5 minutes more, until the sauce thickens slightly and the chicken is cooked through with no pink near the bone and the juices run clear.
Stir through half the tarragon, then scatter the rest over to serve.

tips: Brown the mushrooms until their liquid has gone; this concentrates flavour and stops the sauce tasting watery.
Keep the chicken skin above the liquid while simmering so it stays partly crisp.
Bone-in thighs stay moist during the simmer, whereas breast can dry out.
Add the tarragon at the end, as long cooking dulls its aniseed flavour.
variations: Use flat-leaf parsley and a little thyme instead of tarragon if you don't have any.
Swap the shallots for a small brown onion, finely chopped, and cook for an extra minute.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 2 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat gently in a covered pan until steaming hot throughout.

title: Mexican Pozole Rojo
summary: Hearty pork and hominy soup in a deep red guajillo chilli broth with crunchy fresh toppings.
ingredients: 700 g pork shoulder, cut into 5 cm chunks
800 g canned hominy, drained and rinsed
4 dried chillies (guajillo if available), stems and seeds removed
1 tsp dried oregano, plus extra to serve

stages.title: Soak the chillies
steps: Heat a dry frying pan over medium heat and toast the dried chillies for 20–30 seconds per side, until fragrant and slightly darker; do not let them blacken.
Place the chillies in a heatproof bowl, cover with 500 ml boiling water and soak for 20 minutes, until soft.
Meanwhile, shred the cabbage, slice the radishes and cut the lime into wedges, then set aside for serving.

stages.title: Simmer the pork
steps: Put the pork, half the onion, the stock, the salt and 500 ml water in a large heavy pot and bring to the boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and skim off any foam from the surface with a spoon.
Simmer, partly covered, for 1 hour, until the pork is almost tender and breaks apart easily when pressed with a fork.

stages.title: Blend the chilli sauce
steps: Drain the soaked chillies, discarding the soaking water.
Blend the chillies with the garlic, the remaining onion half, the oregano and 250 ml of the hot pork broth until completely smooth.
Press the purée through a fine sieve into the pot, scraping the underside of the sieve and discarding the skins.

stages.title: Add the hominy and finish
steps: Add the hominy to the pot and stir to combine.
Simmer, partly covered, over medium-low heat for 30 minutes, until the pork is very tender and the broth has deepened in colour.
Lift out the pork, shred it into bite-sized pieces with two forks, discarding any large pieces of fat, and return it to the pot.
Simmer for 5 minutes more, then taste and add more salt if needed.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Ladle the pozole into four bowls, making sure each gets pork and hominy.
Top with the cabbage and radishes, crumble over a pinch of extra oregano and serve with the lime wedges for squeezing.

tips: Toast the chillies only briefly, because scorched chillies turn the broth bitter.
Straining the chilli purée removes the tough skins, giving a smooth, silky broth.
Pork shoulder has enough fat and connective tissue to become tender and enrich the broth; lean cuts turn dry.
Rinsing the canned hominy removes the tinny canning liquid so the broth tastes clean.
variations: Use 700 g bone-in chicken thighs instead of pork and simmer for 40 minutes before shredding, for a lighter broth.
Add 1 tbsp tomato paste to the blender for a slightly sweeter, deeper-red broth.
storage: Refrigerate the pozole in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat gently on the stove until steaming hot throughout, and add the cabbage, radish and lime fresh.

title: Greek Lemon Chicken and Potatoes
summary: Roasted chicken and potatoes soaked in lemon, oregano and garlic, with crisp edges and savoury pan juices.
ingredients: 900 g chicken thighs, bone-in and skin-on
800 g potatoes, peeled and cut into thick wedges

stages.title: Prepare the chicken and potatoes
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Place the potato wedges in a large roasting dish in a single layer.
Place the chicken thighs among the potatoes, skin side up.
Season the chicken and potatoes with the salt and black pepper.

stages.title: Make the lemon dressing
steps: Juice both lemons into a jug to get about 80 ml juice.
Add the olive oil, garlic, oregano, paprika and chicken stock, then whisk to combine.
Pour the dressing evenly over the chicken and potatoes, turning the potatoes to coat them.

stages.title: Roast
steps: Roast for 25 minutes.
Turn the potatoes and spoon the pan juices over the chicken.
Roast for another 20 minutes, until the potatoes are tender when pierced with a knife and the chicken skin is golden.

stages.title: Brown and rest
steps: Increase the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and roast for 10 minutes, until the potato edges are golden and the juices have reduced.
Check the thickest chicken thigh is cooked through, with no pink meat and clear juices.
Rest the dish for 5 minutes, then spoon the pan juices over to serve.

tips: Use a wide dish so the potatoes roast in a single layer. Crowding them makes them steam and turn soft rather than golden.
Bone-in, skin-on thighs stay juicy in the long roast, and the rendered fat flavours the potatoes.
Fresh lemon juice gives a brighter flavour than bottled juice, which can taste flat after roasting.
Turning the potatoes once lets the underside soak up the juices and brown evenly.
variations: Add 1 x 400 g can of artichoke hearts, drained, for the last 20 minutes of roasting.
Scatter 1/2 cup kalamata olives over the dish when you increase the oven temperature.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat in a 180°C oven until the chicken is steaming hot throughout. Potatoes soften when frozen, so freezing is not recommended.

title: Japanese Miso-Glazed Aubergine
summary: Tender roasted aubergine lacquered with sweet-salty miso glaze and finished with toasted sesame.

stages.title: Score the eggplants
steps: Heat the oven to 210°C (190°C fan) and line a large baking tray with baking paper.
Halve the eggplants lengthways, keeping the stalks on if you like.
Score the cut flesh in a diamond pattern about 1 cm deep, taking care not to cut through the skin.
Place the eggplants cut-side up on the tray, brush with the vegetable oil and sprinkle with the salt.

stages.title: Roast the eggplants
steps: Roast on the middle shelf for 25 minutes, until the flesh is very soft and lightly browned.
While they roast, whisk the miso paste, mirin, sugar and soy sauce in a small bowl until smooth and the sugar has dissolved.
Cook the rice according to the packet while the eggplants roast, then keep covered to stay warm.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes, shaking the pan, until golden, then tip onto a plate.

stages.title: Glaze and grill
steps: Switch the oven to grill on high and move the rack to the upper third.
Spread the miso mixture in a thin layer over the hot eggplant flesh.
Grill for 3–4 minutes, watching closely, until the glaze is bubbling and spotted dark brown at the edges.
Take out the tray and rest the eggplants for 2 minutes.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Divide the rice among 4 bowls or plates.
Place the eggplants on top of or alongside the rice.
Scatter over the spring onions and toasted sesame seeds, and serve hot.

tips: Scoring the flesh lets the heat reach the centre and gives the glaze small crevices to sink into, so the eggplant cooks evenly and tastes seasoned throughout.
Add the glaze only for the final grilling, because the sugar and miso scorch and turn bitter if they sit in a hot oven for long.
Roast until the flesh is completely soft and collapsing; undercooked eggplant is spongy and slightly bitter.
Spread the glaze thinly, as a thick layer burns on top before it can heat through.
variations: Use red miso in place of white for a deeper, saltier glaze, and reduce the soy sauce to 2 tsp.
Add 1 tsp grated ginger to the glaze for a sharper, fresher edge.
storage: Refrigerate the eggplant and rice separately in airtight containers for up to 3 days. Reheat the eggplant in a 180°C (160°C fan) oven for 10 minutes until hot through. Not suitable for freezing, as the flesh turns watery.

title: Spanish Albóndigas in Tomato Sauce
summary: Juicy pork-and-beef meatballs simmered in smoky tomato sauce with paprika and garlic.

stages.title: Mix and shape the meatballs
steps: In a large bowl, combine the beef mince, pork mince, egg, breadcrumbs, half the garlic, half the parsley, 3/4 tsp of the salt and the black pepper.
Mix gently with your hands until just combined, as overmixing makes the meatballs tough.
Roll the mixture into about 24 walnut-sized balls, handling lightly and without compacting them.
Place the balls on a tray in a single layer until the pan is hot.

stages.title: Brown the meatballs
steps: Heat 2 tbsp of the olive oil in a large deep frying pan over medium-high heat.
Add half the meatballs and cook for 5–6 minutes, turning occasionally, until browned all over. They will not be cooked through.
Transfer the browned meatballs to a plate.
Brown the remaining meatballs in the same pan for 5–6 minutes, turning occasionally, until browned all over, then transfer to the plate.

stages.title: Make the tomato sauce
steps: Reduce the heat to medium and add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil to the same pan.
Add the onion and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt and cook for 5–6 minutes, stirring often, until soft and translucent.
Add the remaining garlic and the smoked paprika and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the passata and 125 ml water, scraping up the browned bits from the base of the pan.
Bring to a simmer and cook for 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.

stages.title: Simmer and serve
steps: Return the meatballs and any juices on the plate to the pan, nestling them into the sauce.
Partly cover and simmer over low heat for 20–25 minutes, turning the meatballs once, until cooked through with no pink inside and the sauce is thick.
Sprinkle with the remaining parsley and serve with the sliced baguette.

tips: Pork mince alongside beef keeps the meatballs tender and juicy, because the extra fat stops them drying out.
Browning the meatballs first builds a deeper flavour in the sauce, as the caramelised bits dissolve into it.
Smoked paprika gives the sauce its Spanish character; sweet paprika tastes noticeably milder.
Rolling the meatballs without squeezing keeps the texture light, because packed mince turns dense when cooked.
variations: Add 1/2 tsp chilli flakes with the paprika for a spicier, bravas-style sauce.
Stir 1 cup frozen peas into the sauce for the last 5 minutes of simmering.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat gently in a covered pan until steaming hot throughout.

title: Vietnamese Caramelised Pork Bowls
summary: Sticky minced pork cooked with fish sauce, caramel and garlic, served over rice with crisp cucumber.

stages.title: Prepare the aromatics and cucumber
steps: Finely chop the garlic and shallots and keep them together in a small bowl.
Slice the cucumber into thin rounds and cut the lime into wedges.
Measure the brown sugar into a small saucepan and measure the fish sauce into a small jug, ready to use.

stages.title: Cook the rice
steps: Rinse the rice in a sieve under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Cook the rice according to the packet, then keep it covered off the heat until the pork is ready.

stages.title: Make the caramel
steps: Add 1 tbsp water to the brown sugar in the saucepan and heat over medium heat, without stirring, for 3–4 minutes until deep amber.
Stand back and carefully add 3 tbsp warm water, as the caramel will splutter. Stir over low heat for 1 minute until smooth, then stir in the fish sauce and remove from the heat.

stages.title: Cook the pork
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the pork mince and cook for 5–6 minutes, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned and no longer pink.
Add the shallots and garlic and stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the caramel and add the black pepper. Simmer over medium heat for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until the sauce is thick and glossy and clings to the pork.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Divide the rice among four bowls and spoon the pork and its sauce over the top.
Add the cucumber slices and a lime wedge to each bowl, and squeeze the lime over just before eating.

tips: Don't stir the sugar while it caramelises, because stirring can make it crystallise and turn grainy.
Add warm rather than cold water to the caramel so it splutters less and loosens evenly.
Browning the pork well before adding the sauce gives a deeper, savoury base that balances the sweet caramel.
Fish sauce is salty, so taste the pork before serving. Add a squeeze of lime if it tastes too sweet.
variations: Add 1 stalk finely chopped lemongrass with the garlic and shallots for a citrusy note.
Add 1 sliced red chilli with the garlic for a hotter version.
storage: Refrigerate the pork and rice separately in airtight containers for up to 3 days. Reheat the pork in a pan over medium heat with a splash of water until steaming hot throughout. The pork can be frozen for up to 2 months.

title: Tunisian Harissa Baked Fish
summary: Flaky white fish baked over peppers and tomatoes with smoky harissa, cumin and bright lemon.
ingredients: 700 g white fish fillets, firm, cut into 4 portions
2 capsicums, red, deseeded and cut into 2 cm strips
1 red onion, cut into thin wedges
1 lemon, half juiced and half cut into wedges

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Cut the capsicums into strips and the red onion into wedges, and spread them over a large baking tray.
Drizzle the vegetables with 2 tbsp of the olive oil, then add the ground cumin and half the salt and toss to coat.

stages.title: Roast the vegetables
steps: Roast the capsicum and onion on the middle shelf for 10 minutes.
Take the tray out, stir the vegetables so they colour evenly, then roast for another 10 minutes, until softened and starting to colour at the edges.

stages.title: Coat the fish
steps: While the vegetables roast, pat the fish portions dry with paper towel and season with the remaining salt.
Stir the harissa paste with the juice of half the lemon and the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a small bowl.
Brush the harissa mixture all over the fish and leave it at room temperature until the vegetables are ready.

stages.title: Bake the fish
steps: Remove the tray from the oven and push the vegetables aside to make space for the fish.
Nestle the fish among the vegetables and scatter the cherry tomatoes around it.
Return the tray to the oven for 12–15 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily with a fork and the tomatoes have split.

stages.title: Cook the couscous and serve
steps: While the fish bakes, place the couscous in a heatproof bowl, pour over 250 ml boiling water, cover and stand for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Scatter the parsley over the fish and vegetables.
Serve with the couscous and the lemon wedges.

tips: Harissa strength varies a lot between jars, so taste a little first and reduce the amount if it is very hot, as the heat intensifies on the fish.
Patting the fish dry helps the harissa coating cling and brown instead of sliding off in the juices.
Roasting the capsicum and onion first gives them time to soften, since they take longer than the fish to cook.
Thicker fillets need the full 15 minutes, while thin ones can be ready in 12, so check early.
variations: Use salmon fillets instead of white fish and bake until just cooked through and flaking.
Add a drained 400 g can of chickpeas to the tray with the tomatoes for a more filling meal.
storage: Refrigerate the fish and vegetables in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a 160°C (140°C fan) oven until hot through. Not recommended to freeze.

title: Polish Bigos Hunter's Stew
summary: Slow-cooked pork, sausage, sauerkraut and mushrooms in a tangy, deeply savoury cabbage stew.
ingredients: 500 g pork shoulder, trimmed and cut into 3 cm cubes
250 g smoked sausage, sliced 1 cm thick

stages.title: Prepare the ingredients
steps: Pat the pork cubes dry with paper towel and toss with the salt and black pepper.
Slice the sausage, onion and mushrooms, and finely shred the white cabbage.
Drain the sauerkraut in a colander, then taste a strand; if very sharp, rinse it briefly under cold water and squeeze out the excess liquid.

stages.title: Brown the pork
steps: Heat half the oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium-high heat.
Brown the pork in two batches for 4–5 minutes per batch, turning until deeply golden on all sides.
Transfer the pork to a plate, leaving the juices in the pot.

stages.title: Soften the onion and mushrooms
steps: Reduce the heat to medium and add the remaining 1 tbsp oil to the pot.
Cook the onion for 3 minutes, stirring, until soft and starting to colour.
Add the mushrooms and cook for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until they release their liquid and it mostly evaporates.

stages.title: Add the cabbage and sausage
steps: Add the sliced sausage and cook for 2 minutes, stirring, until lightly browned at the edges.
Stir in the white cabbage, sauerkraut, caraway seeds and bay leaves, and cook for 4–5 minutes until the cabbage begins to wilt.

stages.title: Simmer until tender
steps: Return the pork and any plate juices to the pot and pour in the beef stock, scraping up the browned bits from the base.
Bring to a gentle boil over medium-high heat, then reduce the heat to low and cover with the lid.
Simmer for 90 minutes, stirring every 20–30 minutes, until the pork is very tender and breaks apart easily with a fork.

stages.title: Reduce and finish
steps: Remove the lid, raise the heat to medium and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the liquid has reduced and the stew is thick and moist rather than soupy.
Remove the bay leaves and taste, adding a little more salt or black pepper if needed.
Rest off the heat for 5 minutes before serving.

tips: Brown the pork in batches because crowding the pot makes it steam and lose the deep savoury flavour that carries through the stew.
Taste the sauerkraut before deciding whether to rinse it; a quick rinse tames harsh acidity, while unrinsed kraut gives a sharper, more traditional tang.
Cook the stew uncovered at the end so the liquid reduces and the flavours concentrate, giving the thick, rich texture bigos is known for.
Bigos tastes better the next day, as the pork and cabbage absorb more of the smoky, sour flavours while resting.
variations: Soak 10 g dried porcini in 150 ml hot water for 20 minutes, then add the chopped mushrooms and strained soaking liquid in place of 150 ml of the stock.
Stir in 1 tbsp tomato paste with the onion for a slightly sweeter, deeper-red stew.
storage: Cool and refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 4 days, or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat gently in a pot over low heat, adding a splash of water or stock if it has thickened, until steaming hot throughout.

title: Chinese Steamed Ginger Fish
summary: Delicate steamed fish with ginger, spring onions and a sizzling soy-sesame dressing.
ingredients: 50 g ginger, peeled and cut into fine matchsticks
4 spring onions, cut into fine strips
1 tbsp Shaoxing wine or dry sherry

stages.title: Prepare the fish and aromatics
steps: Cut the ginger into fine matchsticks and the spring onions into fine strips, and pick the coriander leaves.
Pat the fish dry with paper towel and rub with the salt.
Lay the fish on a heatproof rimmed plate that fits in your steamer, and scatter half the ginger and half the spring onion over it.
Mix the soy sauce and Shaoxing wine in a small jug and set aside.

stages.title: Steam the fish
steps: Bring about 3 cm of water to a boil in a wok or large pot with a steamer rack, over high heat.
Carefully set the plate on the rack, cover with a lid and reduce the heat to medium so the water keeps boiling steadily.
Steam for 8–10 minutes, depending on thickness, until the fish turns opaque and flakes easily when tested with a fork at the thickest part.
Meanwhile, cook the rice according to the packet.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Lift the plate out carefully and pour away the milky liquid, which can taste fishy.
Scatter the remaining ginger and spring onion over the fish and pour the soy mixture around it.
Heat the vegetable oil in a small saucepan over high heat for 1–2 minutes until it shimmers and just begins to smoke, then pour it over the ginger and spring onion so it sizzles.
Drizzle with the sesame oil, top with the coriander and serve at once with the rice.

tips: Pour away the steaming liquid before dressing, because it tastes fishy and would dilute the sauce.
Hot oil poured over the raw ginger and spring onion releases their fragrance, so make sure the oil is shimmering first.
Thin fillets can be done in 6–7 minutes, so check early; overcooked steamed fish turns dry and firm.
A rimmed plate with a gap around the fish lets steam circulate and cooks it evenly.
variations: Add a thinly sliced red chilli with the ginger on top for heat.
Use a whole 800 g fish, scored on both sides, and steam for 12–15 minutes until the flesh near the bone is opaque.
storage: Best eaten straight away. Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 1 day and reheat gently until steaming hot.

title: American Turkey Meatloaf
summary: Juicy turkey meatloaf with sautéed vegetables and a sticky tomato glaze, sliced thick for dinner.

stages.title: Cook the vegetables
steps: Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
Add the onion and carrot and cook, stirring, for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Tip into a large bowl and cool for 10 minutes so they don't warm the raw mince.

stages.title: Mix and shape the loaf
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Stir the breadcrumbs and milk together in a small bowl and leave for 2 minutes to soak.
Add the turkey mince, egg, soaked breadcrumbs, salt and black pepper to the cooled vegetables and mix gently with your hands until just combined.
Shape into a loaf about 22 cm long on the tray, without packing it tightly.

stages.title: Make the glaze and bake
steps: Whisk the tomato sauce, worcestershire sauce and brown sugar in a small bowl until smooth.
Spread half the glaze over the loaf.
Bake for 35 minutes, until the top is lightly browned.
Spread the remaining glaze over the loaf.

stages.title: Finish and rest
steps: Bake for a further 15–20 minutes, until the glaze is sticky and the centre reaches 74°C on a meat thermometer, or the juices run clear with no pink when you cut into the middle.
Rest the loaf on the tray for 10 minutes before slicing into thick slices.

tips: Turkey mince is lean, so soaking the breadcrumbs in milk keeps the loaf moist.
Cooling the cooked vegetables stops the mince from starting to cook and turning grainy.
Mix gently and don't pack the loaf, as overworking makes it dense.
Resting lets the juices settle so the slices hold together.
variations: Use chicken mince instead of turkey, cooking to the same 74°C centre.
Add 1 tbsp dijon mustard to the glaze for a tangier finish.
storage: Refrigerate slices in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 2 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat until steaming hot throughout.

title: Japanese Onigiri with Tuna Mayo
summary: Soft salted rice triangles stuffed with creamy tuna and wrapped in crisp nori.

stages.title: Rinse and cook the rice
steps: Rinse the rice in a bowl under cold running water, swirling and draining, 4–5 times until the water runs almost clear, then drain well in a sieve for 5 minutes.
Put the rice and 400 ml water in a medium saucepan with a tight-fitting lid and bring to the boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to low, cover and cook for 12 minutes until the water is absorbed and the rice is tender; do not lift the lid.
Remove from the heat and rest, covered, for 10 minutes, then fluff gently with a wet paddle or spoon.

stages.title: Make the tuna mayo filling
steps: Drain the tuna well, pressing out as much liquid as you can, and flake it into a bowl.
Add the mayonnaise and soy sauce and stir until the mixture is creamy and holds together.
Cut the nori sheets in half, then cut each half into 2 strips, to make 12 strips in total.

stages.title: Shape the onigiri
steps: Spread the rice on a tray for about 5 minutes until warm to touch but no longer steaming hot.
Mix the salt with a small bowl of water, wet your hands in it and shake off the excess.
Take about a quarter cup of rice, flatten it in your palm and press a hollow in the centre. Add 1 heaped teaspoon of the tuna filling.
Fold the rice over the filling to enclose it, then press firmly into a triangle with 3 or 4 gentle presses of your cupped hands. Repeat to make 12 onigiri, re-wetting your hands as needed.

stages.title: Wrap and serve
steps: Wrap a strip of nori around the base of each onigiri just before serving so it stays crisp.
Serve at room temperature.

tips: Rinsing until the water is nearly clear removes surface starch so the grains stay separate but still sticky enough to mould.
Use warm rice, not steaming hot, so it is comfortable to handle and clumps together without drying out.
Squeeze the tuna dry before mixing, because extra liquid makes the filling runny and the rice soggy.
Wet, salted hands season the outside of the rice and stop it sticking to your palms.
variations: Replace the tuna with 150 g flaked cooked salmon, mixed with the mayonnaise and soy sauce in the same way.
Roll the finished onigiri in 1 tbsp sesame seeds before wrapping in nori.
storage: Wrap each onigiri in plastic wrap and refrigerate for up to 24 hours, keeping the nori separate. The rice firms up when chilled, so bring to room temperature or microwave for 20–30 seconds before eating. Do not freeze with the mayo filling.

title: Mexican Tostadas de Frijoles
summary: Crunchy corn tortillas layered with creamy refried beans, shredded lettuce, salsa and crumbly cheese.
ingredients: 2 x 400 g cans pinto beans, drained and rinsed

stages.title: Crisp the tortillas
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line two large baking trays with baking paper.
Arrange the tortillas in a single layer on the trays and brush both sides with 1 tbsp of the olive oil.
Bake for 8–10 minutes, turning once halfway, until golden and crisp.
Cool the tortillas on the trays for 5 minutes, as they crisp further while cooling.

stages.title: Cook the beans
steps: Heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a medium frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and ground cumin and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the pinto beans, the salt and 80 ml water. Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the beans are heated through and softened.
Mash the beans roughly with a fork or the back of a wooden spoon, adding a splash more water if needed, until thick and spreadable.
Cover the pan and take it off the heat to keep the beans warm.

stages.title: Prepare the toppings
steps: Shred the lettuce, dice the tomatoes and crumble the feta.
Cut 1 lime into wedges for serving.
Slice the avocado and squeeze the juice of the other lime over it to stop it browning.

stages.title: Assemble and serve
steps: Spread the warm beans evenly over each crisp tortilla.
Top with the lettuce, tomatoes, avocado and feta, then serve straight away with the lime wedges.

tips: Brushing both sides of the tortillas with oil helps them crisp evenly and stay sturdy under the beans.
Mashing the beans while they are warm gives a spreadable layer that acts as a barrier, keeping the tortillas crisp.
Assemble just before eating, as moisture from the beans and tomato softens the tortillas within minutes.
variations: Add 1 finely chopped red chilli with the garlic for a spicier bean layer.
Swap the pinto beans for black beans and use sour cream instead of the feta.
storage: Store the bean mixture and toppings separately in airtight containers in the fridge for up to 3 days, and keep the tortillas in a dry airtight container. Reheat the beans in a pan with a splash of water over medium heat until hot, then assemble fresh.

title: Vietnamese Rice Paper Rolls
summary: Fresh translucent rolls filled with prawns, rice noodles, lettuce and herbs, served with tangy dipping sauce.
ingredients: 1 carrot, peeled and cut into fine matchsticks
1 cucumber, seeded and cut into fine matchsticks
8 lettuce leaves, ribs removed and torn into pieces
300 g cooked prawns, peeled and halved lengthways

stages.title: Cook the vermicelli
steps: Place the rice vermicelli in a heatproof bowl and cover with boiling water from a just-boiled kettle (about 1 litre).
Leave to soak for 5–6 minutes, until soft and no longer opaque.
Drain in a colander, rinse under cold running water to stop the cooking, then drain well and set aside.

stages.title: Prepare the fillings
steps: Cut the carrot and cucumber into fine matchsticks about 8 cm long.
Tear the lettuce into pieces roughly the width of a rice paper sheet.
Pick the mint and coriander leaves and halve the prawns lengthways.
Arrange everything in separate piles near your work area so you can roll quickly.

stages.title: Make the dipping sauce
steps: Combine the hoisin sauce and peanut butter in a small saucepan over low heat.
Stir for 1–2 minutes, until the peanut butter melts and the mixture is smooth.
Remove from the heat and whisk in 80 ml warm water and the lime juice until pourable.
Taste and add a pinch of salt if needed, then pour into a small serving bowl.

stages.title: Roll the rice paper rolls
steps: Half-fill a wide shallow dish with warm tap water and dip one rice paper sheet for 5–10 seconds, until just starting to soften; it will keep softening as you work.
Lay the sheet on a clean damp board and place a piece of lettuce, a small handful of vermicelli, some carrot and cucumber, and a few mint and coriander leaves on the lower third.
Lay 3 prawn halves, cut side up, on the sheet just above the filling so they show through the wrapper.
Fold the bottom edge over the filling, fold in both sides, then roll up tightly until sealed.
Repeat with the remaining sheets and fillings to make 12 rolls, keeping finished rolls covered with a damp tea towel.

tips: Dip rice paper only briefly in warm water, because it keeps softening on the board and over-soaked sheets turn sticky and tear when rolled.
Place the prawns against the wrapper so they show through; it makes tidy rolls and the filling stays in the centre.
Rinse the cooked vermicelli in cold water so the strands stop cooking and don't clump together inside the rolls.
Cover finished rolls with a damp tea towel, as exposed rice paper dries out and turns hard and chewy within minutes.
variations: Swap the prawns for 200 g firm tofu cut into strips and pan-fried in 1 tbsp vegetable oil over medium-high heat for 3–4 minutes per side, until golden.
Use sweet chilli sauce mixed with lime juice as a nut-free dipping sauce.
storage: Best eaten straight away. If needed, wrap each roll in damp paper towel, then cling wrap, and refrigerate for up to 24 hours. Serve cold and do not reheat or freeze.

title: Swedish Overnight Oats with Berries
summary: Creamy chilled oats with yoghurt, cardamom, tart berries and toasted almonds for an easy make-ahead breakfast.
ingredients: 350 ml milk, plus 2–3 tbsp extra to loosen

stages.title: Toast the almonds
steps: Heat a dry frying pan over medium heat.
Add the almonds and toast for 3–4 minutes, shaking the pan often, until golden and fragrant.
Tip the almonds onto a board and cool for 5 minutes, then roughly chop and set aside.

stages.title: Mix the oats
steps: Combine the rolled oats and ground cardamom in a large bowl.
Add the 350 ml milk, the greek yoghurt and the honey, and stir until no dry oats remain.
Divide the mixture evenly between four jars or containers and cover with lids.

stages.title: Chill overnight
steps: Refrigerate the jars for at least 6 hours, or overnight, until the oats have absorbed the liquid and are soft and creamy.
Keep the chopped almonds in a small covered container at room temperature so they stay crisp.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Remove the jars from the fridge and stir each one well.
If the oats are too thick, stir in the extra milk, 1 tbsp at a time, until spoonable.
Top each jar with the blueberries and chopped almonds and serve cold.

tips: Toasting the almonds in a dry pan brings out their oils, giving a deeper nutty flavour and a firmer crunch against soft oats.
Add the almonds just before eating, because moisture from the oats turns them soft within an hour or two.
Greek yoghurt makes a thicker, creamier result than regular yoghurt, which can leave the oats looser.
Stirring in a little extra milk after chilling is needed because the oats keep absorbing liquid in the fridge and thicken overnight.
variations: Swap the blueberries for 1 grated apple and 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon, stirred in before chilling.
Use frozen mixed berries, spooned over the oats the night before so they thaw and release a light juice.
storage: Keep the plain oat mixture covered in the fridge for up to 2 days. Add berries and almonds just before serving. Serve cold; not suited to freezing.

title: Italian Ricotta Pancakes
summary: Light, tender pancakes enriched with ricotta and lemon zest, served with warm berries.

stages.title: Make the ricotta batter
steps: Separate the eggs, putting the whites in a large clean bowl and the yolks in a medium bowl. Finely zest the lemon.
Add the ricotta, milk, 1 tbsp of the caster sugar and the lemon zest to the yolks and whisk for 1 minute until smooth.
Sift the plain flour, baking powder and salt over the ricotta mixture and stir until just combined. A few small lumps are fine.

stages.title: Whip and fold the egg whites
steps: Whisk the egg whites with an electric mixer or balloon whisk for 2–3 minutes until they hold soft peaks.
Fold a third of the whites into the batter to loosen it, then fold in the rest in two batches until no white streaks remain. Stop folding as soon as it is even, to keep the air in.

stages.title: Cook the pancakes
steps: Heat the oven to 120°C (100°C fan) and put a tray inside to keep cooked pancakes warm.
Melt a quarter of the butter in a large non-stick frying pan over medium-low heat until foaming.
Spoon in about 1/4 cup of batter per pancake, leaving space between them. Cook for 2–3 minutes until the surface bubbles and the underside is golden.
Flip and cook for 2–3 minutes more, until golden and the centre springs back when pressed lightly. Move to the oven tray.
Repeat in batches with the remaining butter and batter, making about 12 pancakes. Wipe out the pan between batches if any butter has browned.

stages.title: Warm the berries and serve
steps: Put the blueberries, the remaining 1 tbsp caster sugar and 1 tbsp juice squeezed from the lemon in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Cook for 3–4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the berries soften and release their juices.
Stack the pancakes on plates and spoon the warm berries over just before serving.

tips: Folding the whites in gently keeps the air in, which is what makes these pancakes light rather than dense.
Cook over medium-low heat so the thick batter cooks through in the middle before the outside over-browns.
Use a drained, full-fat ricotta. Wet ricotta adds liquid and makes the pancakes heavy and slow to set.
Leave the pancakes alone once flipped. Pressing them down squeezes out the air you folded in.
variations: Use orange zest instead of lemon, and squeeze orange juice over the berries.
Replace the blueberries with sliced strawberries and cook them for only 2 minutes so they hold their shape.
storage: Cool completely, then refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days or freeze for up to 1 month with baking paper between them. Reheat in a toaster or a 180°C (160°C fan) oven for 5–8 minutes until hot through. Keep the berries separate and eat within 2 days.

title: Greek Yoghurt Honey Bowls
summary: Thick yoghurt topped with floral honey, toasted walnuts and juicy figs for a refreshing breakfast.

stages.title: Toast the walnuts
steps: Heat a dry frying pan over medium-low heat.
Add the walnuts and toast, stirring often, for 3–4 minutes until fragrant and lightly golden.
Tip the walnuts onto a plate and leave to cool for 5 minutes.

stages.title: Prepare the fruit and zest
steps: Finely grate the zest of the orange, then set the zest aside.
Trim the stems from the figs and cut each fig into quarters.
Cut the orange in half and squeeze 1 tbsp juice if you like a looser drizzle, or save the orange for another use.

stages.title: Assemble the bowls
steps: Divide the Greek yoghurt among 4 bowls and smooth the tops with the back of a spoon.
Arrange the fig quarters over the yoghurt and scatter with the cooled walnuts.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Drizzle 1 tbsp honey over each bowl.
Sprinkle with the ground cinnamon and orange zest, then serve straight away.

tips: Toasting the walnuts in a dry pan brings out their oils, which softens their slight bitterness against the sweet honey.
Use thick, strained Greek yoghurt so the figs and nuts sit on top rather than sinking.
Cool the walnuts before topping, as warm nuts will thin the yoghurt and lose their crunch.
Choose figs that give slightly when pressed, as they are sweeter and softer than firm ones.
variations: Swap the figs for sliced peaches or fresh berries when figs are out of season.
Use pepitas in place of the walnuts for a nut-free version.
storage: Best eaten straight away. Keep leftover yoghurt, figs and toasted walnuts separately in the fridge for up to 2 days and assemble just before serving.

title: Spanish Pan con Tomate
summary: Toasted rustic bread rubbed with garlic and ripe tomato, finished with olive oil and flaky salt.
ingredients: 4 thick slices bread, such as sourdough or ciabatta
1/2 tsp salt, flaky if you have it

stages.title: Prepare the tomato
steps: Cut the tomatoes in half across the middle.
Hold a box grater over a bowl and grate the cut side of each tomato until only the skin is left in your hand, then discard the skins.
Stir 1/4 tsp of the salt into the grated tomato and set aside to drain slightly while you toast the bread.

stages.title: Toast the bread
steps: Heat a chargrill pan or large frying pan over medium-high heat for 2 minutes.
Toast the bread for 2–3 minutes per side, until golden with charred marks and crisp outside but still slightly chewy inside.
Transfer the toast to a board while it is still hot.

stages.title: Rub, top and serve
steps: Rub the peeled garlic clove firmly over one side of each slice of hot toast, so the crisp surface grates the garlic into the bread.
Spoon the grated tomato generously over the garlic side of each slice, letting the juices soak in.
Drizzle the olive oil over the toast, sprinkle with the remaining 1/4 tsp salt and serve straight away.

tips: Grate the tomatoes straight onto a bowl rather than the toast so you can drain off excess juice and stop the bread going soggy.
Rub the garlic on while the toast is hot and rough-edged, because it grates the clove and gives a mild flavour; cooled toast takes much less garlic.
Choose very ripe, soft tomatoes, as firm ones grate into watery pulp with little flavour.
variations: Top each slice with thin slices of ham or grated parmesan after adding the tomato for a more filling breakfast.
Add a pinch of paprika with the salt for a gentle smoky flavour.
storage: Best eaten straight away. Leftover grated tomato keeps in the fridge for up to 1 day; toast fresh bread when serving.

title: Italian Marinated Artichokes
summary: Tender artichoke hearts dressed with lemon, parsley, garlic and olive oil for a bright antipasto.

stages.title: Prepare the artichokes
steps: Drain the artichoke hearts in a colander for 5 minutes, then pat them dry with paper towel.
Cut any large artichoke hearts in half or quarters so the pieces are all a similar size.
Place the artichokes in a medium bowl.

stages.title: Prepare the dressing flavours
steps: Finely grate the zest of the lemon, then juice the lemon to give about 2 tbsp juice.
Thinly slice the garlic and finely chop the parsley.
Stir the lemon zest, lemon juice, parsley and salt together in a small bowl.

stages.title: Warm the oil
steps: Heat the olive oil in a small saucepan over low heat, then add the garlic, oregano and chilli flakes.
Cook for 2 minutes, stirring, until the garlic is fragrant and just starting to soften but has not browned.
Remove from the heat and leave to cool for 5 minutes so it is warm, not hot.

stages.title: Marinate and serve
steps: Pour the warm garlic oil into the lemon and parsley mixture and stir to combine.
Pour the dressing over the artichokes and toss gently so the pieces stay whole.
Cover and leave at room temperature for 30 minutes, tossing once halfway through.
Serve at room temperature, spooning over the dressing from the bowl.

tips: Pat the artichokes dry so the dressing coats them instead of being diluted by brine.
Warming the garlic in the oil mellows its raw bite and carries the oregano and chilli flavour through the dressing.
Cool the oil before adding the lemon juice and parsley so the parsley stays bright green and the lemon tastes fresh.
Artichokes packed in brine or water suit this recipe best, as oil-packed ones make the dressing greasy.
variations: Add 1 tbsp drained capers and a handful of chopped kalamata olives with the parsley.
Stir through 1 tbsp chopped mint instead of the oregano for a fresher, brighter flavour.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 4 days. Bring to room temperature before serving. Not suitable to freeze.

title: Chinese Garlic Green Beans
summary: Blistered green beans tossed with sizzling garlic and a savoury soy sauce glaze.

stages.title: Prepare the beans and garlic
steps: Trim the stem ends from the 500 g green beans and cut any very long beans in half.
Wash the beans, then dry them thoroughly with a clean tea towel so they blister rather than steam.
Peel and finely chop the 4 cloves garlic.
In a small bowl, stir the soy sauce and white sugar together until the sugar mostly dissolves.

stages.title: Blister the beans
steps: Heat a wok over high heat for 1 minute, then add 1 tbsp vegetable oil and swirl to coat.
Add half the beans in a single layer and stir-fry for 3–4 minutes, until the skins are wrinkled and blistered with some brown spots and the beans are tender-crisp.
Transfer to a plate, then repeat with the remaining 1 tbsp vegetable oil and the remaining beans, leaving them in the wok after cooking.

stages.title: Add the garlic and glaze
steps: Return the first batch of beans to the wok and reduce the heat to medium.
Push the beans aside, add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant but not browned.
Pour in the soy and sugar mixture, add the salt and toss for 1 minute, until the beans are lightly glazed.
Remove from the heat, drizzle over the sesame oil and toss once. Serve straight away.

tips: Dry beans blister in hot oil instead of steaming, which gives the wrinkled, concentrated texture this dish is known for.
Cooking the beans in two batches keeps the wok hot; crowding it drops the temperature and the beans turn soft and grey.
Add the garlic late and over lower heat because it burns within seconds and turns bitter.
Add the sesame oil off the heat, as high heat dulls its toasty aroma.
variations: Add 1 tbsp chilli flakes with the garlic for a spicy version.
Stir through 2 tbsp roasted peanuts at the end for crunch.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat in a hot pan for 2 minutes. The beans soften, so freezing is not recommended.

title: Greek Tzatziki
summary: Thick yoghurt dip with grated cucumber, garlic, dill and lemon, perfect beside grilled meats.

stages.title: Salt and drain the cucumber
steps: Coarsely grate the cucumber into a bowl, skin on, and toss with 1/4 tsp of the salt.
Leave the cucumber to sit for 10 minutes so the salt draws out the liquid.
Tip the cucumber into a clean tea towel and twist firmly over the sink until it is very dry and no more liquid drips out.

stages.title: Make the garlic paste
steps: Peel the garlic and roughly chop it.
Sprinkle over the remaining 1/4 tsp salt and crush with the flat side of a knife, or use a mortar and pestle, until a smooth paste forms.

stages.title: Combine the tzatziki
steps: Spoon the Greek yoghurt into a medium bowl and stir until smooth.
Add the squeezed cucumber, the garlic paste, the chopped dill and the lemon juice.
Stir until evenly combined, then taste and add a little more lemon juice if you want it sharper.

stages.title: Chill and serve
steps: Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 20 minutes so the garlic mellows and the flavours blend.
Stir again, spoon into a serving bowl and drizzle with the olive oil just before serving.

tips: Salting and squeezing the cucumber stops it releasing water later, which keeps the tzatziki thick instead of runny.
Use full-fat Greek yoghurt for a creamy, thick dip; low-fat versions tend to be thinner and more tart.
Crushing the garlic with salt breaks it into a smooth paste, so you don't get harsh raw chunks.
Start with one clove of garlic if you prefer a gentler flavour, as it strengthens as the dip sits.
variations: Replace half the dill with 1 tbsp finely chopped mint for a fresher, cooler flavour.
Stir in 1 tsp red wine vinegar instead of the lemon juice for a more traditional tang.
storage: Keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Stir before serving, as a little liquid may separate. Not suitable for freezing.

title: French Pear Tarte Tatin
summary: Caramelised pears baked beneath buttery puff pastry and turned out into a glossy upside-down tart.

stages.title: Prepare the pears and pastry
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and take the puff pastry out to thaw if it is still frozen.
Peel the pears, cut them in half lengthways and scoop out the cores with a teaspoon.
Juice half the lemon over the pears and toss to coat so they don't brown.
Cut a round from the pastry about 2 cm wider than a 24 cm ovenproof frying pan and prick it all over with a fork.

stages.title: Make the caramel
steps: Sprinkle the caster sugar evenly over the base of a 24 cm ovenproof frying pan and heat over medium heat without stirring until it melts and turns deep amber, 6–8 minutes, swirling the pan occasionally.
Take the pan off the heat and add the butter, swirling until melted and smooth. Stand back as it will spit.
Stir in the vanilla extract.

stages.title: Soften the pears
steps: Arrange the pear halves in the caramel, cut-side up, packing them in snugly.
Cook over medium heat for 8–10 minutes, spooning the caramel over the pears, until the caramel is bubbling and thick and the pears have softened slightly.
Remove the pan from the heat and let the bubbling settle for 1 minute.

stages.title: Bake
steps: Lay the pastry over the pears and tuck the edges down around the fruit inside the pan.
Bake on the middle shelf for 25–30 minutes, until the pastry is puffed, deep golden and crisp.

stages.title: Rest and turn out
steps: Rest the tart in the pan for 5 minutes so the caramel thickens slightly but does not set.
Run a knife around the edge, place a large plate over the pan and, wearing oven mitts, flip it in one quick movement.
Lift off the pan and rearrange any pears that have shifted, then serve warm.

tips: Firm pears hold their shape through the caramel and the bake; soft, ripe pears turn to mush.
Don't stir the sugar as it melts, because stirring can make it crystallise. Swirl the pan to even out the colour instead.
Resting for 5 minutes lets the caramel thicken so it clings to the pears; turned out straight away it runs off, and left too long it sticks to the pan.
Tucking the pastry edges inside the pan keeps the caramel from bubbling out and gives the tart a neat rim once it is inverted.
variations: Add a pinch of ground cardamom to the sugar before melting for a warmly spiced caramel.
Swap the pears for 4 firm apples, and cook them in the caramel for 12 minutes before adding the pastry.
storage: Best eaten warm on the day. Leftovers keep in the fridge for up to 2 days; reheat slices in a 160°C (140°C fan) oven for 10 minutes to crisp the pastry. Not suitable for freezing.

title: Indian Kheer Rice Pudding
summary: Creamy slow-simmered rice pudding scented with cardamom, saffron and toasted pistachios.

stages.title: Soak the rice and prepare the flavourings
steps: Rinse the rice in a sieve under cold running water until the water runs mostly clear.
Cover the rice with cold water in a bowl and soak for 15 minutes, then drain well.
While the rice soaks, lightly crush the cardamom pods with the flat of a knife so they split open.
Roughly chop the pistachios and set aside.

stages.title: Simmer the milk with the rice
steps: Pour the milk into a large heavy-based saucepan and heat over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until small bubbles form around the edge, about 8 minutes.
Add the drained rice, crushed cardamom pods and saffron threads, and stir well.
Bring back to a gentle simmer, about 5 minutes, then reduce the heat to low.

stages.title: Cook until thick and creamy
steps: Cook over low heat for 35 minutes, stirring every 3–4 minutes and scraping the base of the pan so the milk does not catch.
When the rice is very soft and the milk has reduced to a thick, creamy consistency, stir in the sugar.
Cook for a further 5 minutes over low heat, stirring constantly, until the sugar has dissolved and the kheer coats the back of a spoon.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Remove the pan from the heat and fish out the cardamom pods.
Stir in the rosewater and let the kheer rest for 10 minutes; it will thicken further as it cools.
Spoon into 4 bowls and scatter with the chopped pistachios. Serve warm.

tips: Soaking the rice softens the grains so they break down and release starch, which thickens the kheer without any cornflour.
Use a heavy-based saucepan and keep the heat low, as thin pans let the milk scorch on the base and give a burnt taste.
Add the sugar only after the rice is soft, because sugar added earlier can keep the grains firm.
Add the rosewater off the heat, as its delicate fragrance fades with prolonged cooking.
variations: Use chopped almonds instead of pistachios, toasted in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes until lightly golden.
Replace the sugar with 2 tbsp honey stirred in off the heat for a softer sweetness.
storage: To serve cold, cover and chill for at least 2 hours after resting. Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. It thickens when cold, so stir in a splash of milk and reheat gently over low heat, or serve chilled. Not suitable for freezing as the texture turns grainy.

title: American Peach Cobbler
summary: Juicy cinnamon peaches baked beneath a golden, tender biscuit topping and served warm.
ingredients: 800 g peaches, stones removed and cut into 1 cm slices
80 g butter, cold and cut into small cubes

stages.title: Prepare the peach filling
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan) and place a rack in the centre.
Put the sliced peaches in a 1.5 litre baking dish.
Add half the sugar (50 g), the lemon juice and the cinnamon, then toss until the peaches are evenly coated.

stages.title: Make the topping dough
steps: Whisk the flour, baking powder and the remaining 50 g sugar in a large bowl.
Rub the cold butter into the flour mixture with your fingertips until it looks like coarse crumbs with a few pea-sized pieces.
Pour in the milk and stir with a fork just until a soft, sticky dough forms. Stop mixing as soon as no dry flour remains.

stages.title: Assemble and bake
steps: Drop heaped spoonfuls of dough over the peaches, leaving small gaps so steam can escape.
Bake in the oven for 35–40 minutes, until the topping is deep golden and a skewer inserted into the centre of a dumpling comes out clean.
Check that the peach juices are bubbling thickly around the edges of the dish. If the topping browns too quickly, cover loosely with foil for the last 10 minutes.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Rest the cobbler for 10 minutes so the hot juices thicken slightly.
Spoon into bowls, scooping up plenty of the juices from the base.

tips: Use ripe but firm peaches, because very soft fruit breaks down into a watery mush under the topping.
Keep the butter cold so it melts in the oven and creates a tender, crumbly topping rather than a dense one.
Leave gaps between the dough spoonfuls so steam escapes and the underside of the topping cooks through instead of turning gluey.
Resting for 10 minutes lets the juices thicken so they cling to the fruit rather than running out.
variations: Use nectarines or firm plums instead of peaches, adding an extra 1 tbsp sugar for tart plums.
Sprinkle 1 tbsp extra sugar over the dough before baking for a crunchy, sugared crust.
storage: Cool completely, then cover and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Reheat portions at 160°C (140°C fan) for 15 minutes, or in the microwave until hot.

title: French Clafoutis with Cherries
summary: Juicy cherries baked in a delicate vanilla custard batter with lightly crisp edges.

stages.title: Prepare the dish and cherries
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan).
Grease a 1.5 litre shallow baking dish with the softened butter.
Pit the cherries and scatter them in a single layer over the base of the dish.

stages.title: Make the batter
steps: Whisk the eggs and caster sugar in a large bowl for 1–2 minutes until pale and slightly thickened.
Whisk in the plain flour and salt until no dry flour remains.
Gradually whisk in the milk, then the melted butter and vanilla extract, until the batter is smooth and thin like pouring cream.
Rest the batter for 5 minutes so the flour hydrates.

stages.title: Bake the clafoutis
steps: Pour the batter slowly over the cherries so they stay spread out.
Bake in the middle of the oven for 35–40 minutes until puffed, golden on top and just set, with only a slight wobble in the centre.
Test by inserting a knife into the centre; it should come out clean apart from a little cherry juice.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Rest the clafoutis in the dish for 10–15 minutes; it will sink slightly as it cools, which is normal.
Dust with the icing sugar through a fine sieve just before serving.
Serve warm or at room temperature, cut into wedges.

tips: Leaving the pits in is traditional and adds a subtle almond note, but pitting makes it safe and easy to eat, so warn guests if you keep them.
Resting the batter lets the flour absorb the milk, giving a tender custard rather than a rubbery one.
Take the clafoutis out as soon as the centre is just set; overbaking turns the custard dry and eggy.
Dust with icing sugar only at the end, as it dissolves into the surface if added while hot.
variations: Replace the cherries with 450 g halved and stoned apricots, cut side down, when cherries are out of season.
Replace 1 tsp of the vanilla with 1 tbsp of kirsch for a more traditional flavour.
storage: Cover and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Eat cold or reheat individual portions at 160°C for 10 minutes. Not suitable for freezing as the custard turns watery.

title: Mexican Churros with Chocolate Sauce
summary: Crisp cinnamon-sugar churros with soft centres, dipped into warm dark chocolate sauce.

stages.title: Make the dough
steps: Combine the water, butter and salt in a medium saucepan and heat over medium heat, stirring, until the butter melts and the water comes to a boil.
Tip in the flour all at once and reduce the heat to low. Stir vigorously with a wooden spoon for 1–2 minutes, until the dough forms a smooth ball and pulls away from the sides of the pan.
Transfer the dough to a bowl and cool for 5 minutes, until warm but not hot to the touch.

stages.title: Beat in the eggs and pipe
steps: Beat the eggs and vanilla extract together in a small jug. Add to the dough in 3 additions, beating hard with a wooden spoon or electric beaters after each, until the dough is thick, glossy and smooth.
Spoon the dough into a piping bag fitted with a large star nozzle.
Line a tray with baking paper and pipe 10–12 cm lengths onto it, snipping each with scissors. You should have about 12 churros.

stages.title: Make the chocolate sauce
steps: Place the chocolate in a heatproof bowl.
Heat the cream in a small saucepan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes, until steaming and small bubbles form at the edge. Do not let it boil.
Pour the hot cream over the chocolate and stand for 1 minute, then stir until smooth and glossy. Keep warm.

stages.title: Fry and coat
steps: Mix the caster sugar and ground cinnamon on a shallow plate.
Heat the vegetable oil in a deep, heavy-based saucepan over medium heat to 175°C, or until a small piece of dough sizzles steadily and turns golden in about 1 minute.
Fry 4 churros at a time for 3–4 minutes, turning occasionally, until deep golden and cooked through. Cut one open to check the inside is cooked and not doughy.
Lift out with tongs, drain on paper towel for 30 seconds, then roll in the cinnamon sugar. Repeat with the remaining dough, letting the oil return to 175°C between batches.
Serve the churros hot with the warm chocolate sauce for dipping.

tips: Beating the eggs in a little at a time lets the dough absorb them. It stays thick enough to hold the ridges when piped.
Oil at 175°C cooks the centre before the outside darkens. Cooler oil gives greasy churros, and hotter oil leaves them raw inside.
Fry in small batches so the oil temperature doesn't drop and the churros don't stick together.
The star nozzle makes ridges that crisp up and give the cinnamon sugar more to cling to.
variations: Stir 1 tsp finely grated orange zest into the cream before heating for an orange chocolate sauce.
Add a pinch of chilli powder to the chocolate sauce for a gentle warmth.
storage: Churros are best eaten within 30 minutes of frying. Refrigerate leftover sauce in a sealed container for up to 3 days and reheat gently in the microwave in short bursts, stirring.

title: Greek Portokalopita
summary: Syrup-soaked orange and yoghurt cake made with crisp filo pieces and fragrant citrus zest.

stages.title: Dry the filo
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Tear the filo pastry sheets into rough 3–4 cm pieces and spread them over the tray.
Bake for 10–12 minutes until dry and crisp but not coloured.
Cool the filo on the tray for 20 minutes, then crush any large pieces slightly with your hands.

stages.title: Make the batter
steps: Grease a 20 cm square or round cake tin with the 1 tsp olive oil and line the base with baking paper.
Finely grate the zest of 2 oranges, then juice those 2 oranges and set the juice aside for the syrup.
Whisk the eggs and 100 g of the sugar in a large bowl for 2 minutes until pale and slightly thick.
Whisk in the Greek yoghurt, the 150 ml olive oil, the orange zest, the vanilla extract and the baking powder until smooth.
Fold in the cooled filo until every piece is coated, then pour the mixture into the tin and level the top.

stages.title: Bake the cake and make the syrup
steps: Bake the cake in the oven at 180°C (160°C fan) for 40–45 minutes, until the top is deep golden and a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean. Cover loosely with foil if it browns too fast.
While the cake bakes, juice the remaining orange and combine it with the reserved orange juice, the remaining 150 g sugar and the 200 ml water in a saucepan.
Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves, then simmer for 8–10 minutes until lightly syrupy.
Take the syrup off the heat and leave it to cool to warm while the cake finishes.

stages.title: Soak and serve
steps: Leave the cake in its tin on a wire rack for 10 minutes, until warm rather than hot.
Pour the warm syrup slowly over the cake, a little at a time so it soaks in evenly.
Let the cake absorb the syrup for 30 minutes, then cut into 4 portions.

tips: Drying the filo makes it absorb the batter evenly, so the cake is moist and tender rather than gluey.
Pour warm syrup over a warm cake: if both are hot the cake turns soggy, and if both are cold the syrup sits on top.
Zest the oranges before juicing them, because the zest holds most of the orange flavour and is hard to grate from a squeezed fruit.
variations: Add a cinnamon stick and 2 strips of orange peel to the syrup while it simmers, then remove them before pouring.
Serve each portion with an extra spoonful of Greek yoghurt and a little orange zest.
storage: Keep covered at room temperature for 1 day, or refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 4 days. Serve at room temperature or warm briefly in the microwave.

title: Australian Anzac Biscuits
summary: Golden oat-and-coconut biscuits with crisp edges, chewy centres and rich golden syrup flavour.

stages.title: Prepare the dry mix
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C (150°C fan) and line two large baking trays with baking paper.
Combine the rolled oats, plain flour, desiccated coconut and brown sugar in a large bowl.
Stir with a fork, breaking up any lumps of sugar, then make a well in the centre.

stages.title: Make the butter mixture
steps: Melt the butter and golden syrup in a small saucepan over low heat, stirring, for 2–3 minutes until smooth.
Stir the bicarbonate soda into the boiling water in a small cup, then pour it into the butter mixture. It will foam up.
Remove the pan from the heat straight away.

stages.title: Mix and shape
steps: Pour the foaming butter mixture into the well in the dry ingredients.
Stir until the mixture is evenly moistened and holds together when pressed.
Roll heaped tablespoons of mixture into balls, each about 3 cm wide, to make about 20.

stages.title: Bake and cool
steps: Place the balls on the trays, spaced 5 cm apart, and flatten each to about 1 cm thick.
Bake for 12–15 minutes, swapping the trays halfway, until deep golden brown around the edges.
Cool on the trays for 10 minutes, as the biscuits are soft when hot and firm up as they cool, then transfer to a wire rack.

tips: Rolled oats give chew and texture; instant oats turn the biscuits pasty.
Dissolving the bicarbonate soda in boiling water and adding it to the warm butter makes the mixture foam, which helps the biscuits spread and gives a crisp edge.
Bake a few minutes longer for crisp biscuits, or take them out at the lighter golden stage for chewy centres.
Leave space on the trays, as the biscuits spread while baking.
variations: Add 1 tsp finely grated orange zest to the dry ingredients for a citrus note.
Dip cooled biscuits halfway into melted dark chocolate and let it set on baking paper.
storage: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 5 days. Freeze for up to 2 months.

title: American Banana Cream Pie
summary: Buttery biscuit crust filled with sliced bananas and vanilla custard, crowned with whipped cream.

stages.title: Make the biscuit crust
steps: Crush the digestive biscuits to fine crumbs in a food processor, or in a zip-lock bag with a rolling pin.
Melt the butter in a small saucepan over low heat for 2–3 minutes, then stir it through the crumbs until they look like wet sand.
Press the crumbs firmly over the base and up the sides of a 20 cm pie dish, using the back of a spoon or a flat-bottomed glass.
Chill the crust in the fridge for 30 minutes, until firm.

stages.title: Cook the custard
steps: Heat the milk in a medium saucepan over medium heat for 4–5 minutes, until steaming and small bubbles appear at the edge. Do not let it boil.
Whisk the egg yolks, caster sugar and cornflour in a large heatproof bowl for 1–2 minutes, until pale and smooth.
Pour the hot milk into the yolk mixture in a thin stream, whisking constantly so the eggs don't scramble.
Return the mixture to the saucepan over medium heat and stir constantly with a whisk for 4–5 minutes, until thick and bubbling. Keep stirring for 1 minute more to cook out the cornflour.
Remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla extract.

stages.title: Cool the custard and fill the pie
steps: Pour the custard into a clean bowl, then press cling film directly onto the surface to stop a skin forming. Cool for 10 minutes.
Peel and slice 2 of the bananas into 5 mm rounds and layer them over the chilled crust.
Pour the warm custard over the bananas and smooth the top with a spatula.

stages.title: Chill until set
steps: Press fresh cling film lightly onto the surface of the custard.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, until the custard is completely set and holds a clean slice.

stages.title: Top and serve
steps: Whip the thickened cream in a bowl with a whisk or electric beaters for 2–3 minutes, until soft peaks form.
Spread the cream over the set custard, swirling it into peaks.
Slice the remaining banana and arrange it on top just before serving so it doesn't brown.
Cut into 4 wedges with a sharp knife, wiping the blade between cuts.

tips: Pressing cling film onto the custard stops a rubbery skin from forming, which would leave lumps under the cream.
Cooking the custard for a full minute after it bubbles cooks out the starchy taste of the cornflour and ensures it sets firmly.
Pouring the hot milk into the yolks slowly warms them gently, so the eggs thicken the custard instead of scrambling.
Add the fresh banana garnish only at serving; cut banana browns within an hour or two.
variations: Scatter toasted desiccated coconut over the whipped cream for a nutty crunch.
Drizzle a little warm dulce de leche-style caramel over the bananas before adding the custard.
storage: Refrigerate covered for up to 2 days, though the crust softens over time. Not suitable to freeze, as the custard will weep when thawed.

title: Peruvian Aji de Gallina
summary: Shredded chicken in a creamy yellow chilli and walnut sauce, served with rice and olives.
ingredients: 3 slices white bread, crusts removed, torn

stages.title: Poach the chicken
steps: Put the chicken breast and chicken stock in a medium saucepan and add 400 ml water so the chicken is covered.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then reduce to low and poach for 15–18 minutes, until cooked through, no longer pink in the middle and 75°C in the thickest part.
Lift the chicken onto a board and rest for 10 minutes, keeping the broth in the pan.
Shred the chicken with two forks and set aside.

stages.title: Make the walnut sauce base
steps: Put the torn bread in a bowl, pour over the evaporated milk and soak for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the bread and milk, walnuts, parmesan and 250 ml of the reserved warm broth to a blender.
Blend for 1 minute until completely smooth, and set aside.

stages.title: Cook the aji sauce
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large deep frying pan over medium heat and cook the onion with the salt for 5–6 minutes, until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic, aji amarillo paste and turmeric and stir for 2 minutes, until fragrant.
Pour in the blended sauce and stir well, then simmer over low heat for 8–10 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy enough to coat a spoon.
Stir in a splash more reserved broth if the sauce becomes too thick.

stages.title: Cook the rice and eggs
steps: Cook the rice according to the packet.
