While the rice cooks, put the eggs in a small saucepan of boiling water and boil over medium heat for 10 minutes, until the yolks are firm and cooked through.
Cool the eggs under cold running water, then peel and cut into quarters.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Fold the shredded chicken into the sauce and warm through over low heat for 3–4 minutes, until hot all the way through.
Season with black pepper and extra salt if needed.
Spoon the chicken over the rice and top with the egg quarters and kalamata olives.

tips: Add the aji amarillo paste gradually and taste, because brands vary a lot in heat.
Poaching the chicken gently keeps the breast tender, while a hard boil makes it stringy.
Using the poaching broth to thin the sauce adds chicken flavour that plain water would not.
Blending the soaked bread with the walnuts is what thickens the sauce, so blend until no grit remains.
variations: Replace the walnuts with the same amount of pecans for a slightly sweeter sauce.
Use poached chicken thigh instead of breast for richer, more tender meat, poaching for 20–25 minutes until cooked through.
storage: Refrigerate the chicken sauce in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat gently in a saucepan over low heat with a splash of water or stock until steaming hot. Keep the rice and eggs separate; freezing is not recommended because the sauce can split.

title: Thai Larb Gai
summary: Warm minced chicken salad with lime, fish sauce, mint and toasted rice powder.
ingredients: 1 bunch coriander, leaves and tender stems roughly chopped

stages.title: Make the toasted rice powder
steps: Heat a dry frying pan over medium heat and add the 2 tbsp rice.
Toast, shaking the pan often, for 4–5 minutes until deep golden and fragrant.
Tip the rice onto a plate and cool for 3 minutes.
Grind the rice in a mortar or spice grinder to a coarse powder, like fine sand with some texture.

stages.title: Prepare the dressing and herbs
steps: Juice 2 of the limes to get about 80 ml juice and cut the remaining lime into wedges for serving.
Thinly slice the shallots and pick the mint leaves.
Roughly chop the coriander and separate the lettuce leaves, then keep them cold until serving.
Stir the fish sauce and lime juice together in a small bowl.

stages.title: Cook the chicken
steps: Heat a large frying pan over medium-high heat and add the chicken mince with 60 ml water.
Cook for 7–8 minutes, breaking up the mince with a wooden spoon, until cooked through and no longer pink, and most of the liquid has evaporated.
Take the pan off the heat and let the mince cool for 2 minutes.

stages.title: Toss and serve
steps: Pour the fish sauce and lime mixture over the warm chicken and stir through the chilli flakes and shallots.
Fold in the toasted rice powder, mint and coriander.
Taste and add a little more fish sauce or lime if needed.
Spoon the larb into the lettuce leaves and serve with the lime wedges.

tips: Toasting the rice until deep golden gives the nutty flavour and slightly crunchy texture that larb is known for.
Cooking the mince with a little water keeps the small crumbs tender and stops them drying out.
Add the herbs and shallots once the chicken has cooled slightly so they stay fresh and don't wilt.
variations: Use pork mince for larb moo, cooked until no pink remains.
Add 1 tsp sugar and extra chilli flakes for a sweeter, hotter version.
storage: Refrigerate the chicken mixture in an airtight container for up to 2 days, keeping the lettuce separate. Serve cold or reheat until steaming hot throughout.

title: Italian Ribollita
summary: Rustic Tuscan bean-and-vegetable soup thickened with bread, kale and olive oil.
ingredients: 1 x 400 g can cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
200 g kale, stems removed and leaves sliced
200 g stale bread, torn into 2 cm pieces

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables and bread
steps: Finely dice the onion, carrots and celery into pieces about 5 mm wide so they soften evenly.
Crush the garlic and pick the thyme leaves from the sprigs.
Remove the kale stems, then slice the leaves into 2 cm strips.
Tear the stale bread into 2 cm pieces and drain and rinse the cannellini beans.

stages.title: Soften the soffritto
steps: Heat 2 tbsp of the olive oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium heat.
Add the onion, carrots, celery and salt, and cook for 10 minutes, stirring often, until soft and the onion is translucent.
Stir in the garlic and thyme leaves and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

stages.title: Simmer the soup
steps: Mash half the cannellini beans with a fork until mostly smooth.
Add the diced tomatoes, vegetable stock, mashed beans and the remaining whole beans to the pot, and bring to the boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer for 15 minutes, until the vegetables are very tender.
Stir in the kale and simmer for 8 minutes, until the leaves are dark and tender.

stages.title: Add the bread and rest
steps: Stir the torn bread into the soup, take the pot off the heat and leave for 15 minutes, until the bread has swollen and the soup is thick and stew-like.
Return the pot to low heat and warm for 5 minutes, stirring to break up the bread, until steaming hot.
Season with black pepper and extra salt if needed, then drizzle each serving with some of the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil.

tips: Stale bread holds its shape while it soaks up the broth, whereas fresh bread turns to paste.
Mashing half the beans thickens the soup naturally and gives a creamy base without cream.
Cooking the soffritto slowly for the full 10 minutes draws out the sweetness that carries the soup, since there is no meat.
Ribollita means reboiled and tastes better the next day, because the bread continues to thicken the soup as it sits.
variations: Swap the kale for cavolo nero, which is the traditional Tuscan green, and cook it for an extra 2–3 minutes.
Add a parmesan rind with the stock and remove it before serving for a savoury depth (parmesan is not vegetarian, so check the label if serving vegetarians).
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. The soup thickens as it sits, so add a splash of water when reheating in a pot over medium heat until steaming hot. Freeze for up to 2 months.

title: Indian Baingan Bharta
summary: Smoky mashed aubergine cooked with onion, tomato, ginger and green chilli.

stages.title: Roast the eggplants
steps: Heat the oven to 230°C (210°C fan) and line a tray with baking paper.
Prick each eggplant 5–6 times with a fork and rub the skins with 1 tbsp of the oil.
Roast for 35–40 minutes, turning once, until the skins are blackened and wrinkled and the flesh is completely soft when pressed.

stages.title: Cool and mash the flesh
steps: Rest the eggplants on the tray for 10 minutes, until cool enough to handle.
Slit them open, scoop out the soft flesh and discard the skins and any pooled bitter liquid.
Chop the flesh roughly with a knife until mashed but still a little chunky.

stages.title: Cook the spiced base
steps: Heat the remaining 2 tbsp oil in a large frying pan over medium heat and add the cumin seeds. Cook for 30 seconds until they sizzle and smell fragrant.
Add the onion and cook, stirring, for 6–7 minutes until soft and golden.
Stir in the garlic, ginger and green chilli and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, turmeric and salt. Cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring often, until the tomatoes break down into a thick, jammy paste.

stages.title: Combine and finish
steps: Add the mashed eggplant to the pan and stir through the tomato base.
Cook over medium-low heat for 8 minutes, stirring often, until thick and the oil begins to separate at the edges.
Stir through the coriander and taste for salt. Serve hot.

tips: Charring the skins until blackened gives the dish its smoky flavour; pale skins mean a flat-tasting bharta.
Discard the liquid that collects inside the roasted eggplants, as it tastes bitter and makes the dish watery.
Cook the tomatoes until jammy before adding the eggplant so the finished bharta is thick, not soupy.
variations: Hold the eggplants directly over a gas flame, turning with tongs for 10–12 minutes until blackened and collapsed, for a stronger smoky flavour.
Stir in 1/2 cup frozen peas with the eggplant and cook until heated through for a sweeter finish.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat in a pan over low heat until steaming hot, adding a splash of water if thick.

title: German Kartoffelsalat
summary: Warm potato salad dressed with tangy mustard, vinegar and bacon instead of mayonnaise.
ingredients: 1/2 tsp salt, plus extra for the cooking water

stages.title: Cook the potatoes
steps: Scrub the potatoes and leave them whole and unpeeled. Place in a large pot, cover with cold water and add a generous pinch of salt.
Bring to the boil over high heat, then reduce to medium and simmer for 20–25 minutes, until a knife slides into the centre of the largest potato with no resistance.
Drain and leave until cool enough to handle, about 5 minutes. Peel the potatoes while still warm, then cut into 5 mm slices and place in a large bowl.

stages.title: Make the bacon dressing
steps: Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Add the bacon and cook for 5–6 minutes, stirring, until golden and crisp.
Add the onion to the pan and cook in the bacon fat for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent.
Pour in the stock, vinegar, mustard and sugar. Whisk, scraping up any browned bits, and simmer for 2 minutes until slightly reduced.
Stir in the salt and a good grind of black pepper.

stages.title: Dress and rest
steps: Pour the hot dressing over the warm potato slices and fold gently with a large spoon so the slices stay whole.
Leave to sit at room temperature for 15–20 minutes, folding once halfway, until the potatoes have absorbed most of the liquid.
Taste and add salt or a splash more vinegar if needed. Fold through the parsley and serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: Waxy potatoes hold their shape when sliced and tossed, whereas floury varieties break down into mash.
Peeling and slicing the potatoes while warm lets them soak up the dressing; cold potatoes absorb far less flavour.
Starting the potatoes in cold water cooks them evenly, so the outsides don't turn mushy before the centres are tender.
variations: For a vegetarian version, leave out the bacon, cook the onion in 2 tbsp olive oil and check the stock and mustard labels.
Add 2 chopped gherkins and 1 tbsp of their brine to the dressing for a sharper flavour.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Bring to room temperature before serving, or warm gently in a pan. Not suitable for freezing.

title: Chinese Tomato Egg Stir-Fry
summary: Soft scrambled eggs folded into juicy sweet-savoury tomatoes for a quick homestyle meal.
ingredients: 3 spring onions, thinly sliced, white and green parts separated

stages.title: Cook the rice
steps: Cook the rice according to the packet, so it is ready when the stir-fry is finished.
While the rice cooks, beat the eggs in a bowl with 1/4 tsp of the salt until the whites and yolks are fully combined.
Cut the tomatoes into wedges and slice the spring onions, keeping the white and green parts separate.

stages.title: Prepare the sauce
steps: Mix the cornflour with 1 tbsp water in a small bowl until smooth.
Measure the sugar and soy sauce into a small bowl so they are ready to add.
Keep the rice covered and warm once cooked.

stages.title: Scramble the eggs
steps: Heat half the oil in a wok over medium-high heat for 1 minute until it shimmers.
Pour in the eggs and leave for 10 seconds, then gently push them from the edges to the centre.
Cook for 1–2 minutes until the eggs are just set but still soft and slightly wet in places, then transfer to a plate.

stages.title: Cook the tomatoes
steps: Add the remaining oil to the wok over medium-high heat and stir-fry the spring onion whites for 20 seconds until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt and cook, stirring often, for 3–4 minutes until they soften and release their juices.
Stir in the sugar and soy sauce and cook for 1 minute.
Stir the cornflour mixture, pour it in and cook for 30 seconds until the sauce thickens slightly and turns glossy.

stages.title: Combine and serve
steps: Return the eggs to the wok and fold gently through the tomatoes for 1 minute until the eggs are cooked through and no longer wet.
Scatter over the spring onion greens and serve straight away with the rice.

tips: Take the eggs out while they are still soft, because they finish cooking when folded back into the hot tomatoes.
Cooking the eggs in hot oil makes them puff up and stay tender rather than turning rubbery.
Ripe tomatoes give the best sauce, and the sugar balances their acidity if yours are tart.
variations: Add 1 tsp sesame oil just before serving for a nutty aroma.
Use 2 tbsp tomato paste with a splash of water if your tomatoes are pale and lack flavour.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a pan or microwave until steaming hot. Not recommended to freeze, as the eggs turn watery.

title: Egyptian Ful Medames
summary: Warm mashed fava beans with cumin, lemon, garlic and olive oil, scooped up with flatbread.

stages.title: Prepare the toppings
steps: Finely chop the tomatoes and discard the watery seeds if very wet.
Pick and finely chop the parsley leaves.
Crush the garlic with the salt into a rough paste.
Juice the lemons; you need about 80 ml juice.

stages.title: Simmer the beans
steps: Tip the fava beans and their liquid from both cans into a medium saucepan.
Add 100 ml water and bring to a simmer over medium heat, then cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the beans are hot and the liquid has reduced slightly.
Stir in the ground cumin and black pepper and cook for 1 minute.

stages.title: Mash and season
steps: Reduce the heat to low and mash about half the beans against the side of the pan with a fork or the back of a wooden spoon, leaving the rest whole.
Stir in the garlic paste, 1 tbsp of the olive oil and two-thirds of the lemon juice.
Simmer for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until thick and creamy but still spoonable; add a splash of water if it looks dry.

stages.title: Warm the bread and serve
steps: Warm the pita bread in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 1 minute each side, until soft and lightly toasted.
Divide the beans among four bowls.
Top with the tomatoes, parsley and chilli flakes, then drizzle with the remaining 2 tbsp olive oil and the remaining lemon juice.
Serve straight away with the warm pita bread.

tips: Canned fava beans are already cooked, so a short simmer is enough to heat them and thicken the liquid; longer cooking turns them dry and dull.
Mashing only half the beans makes a creamy base while keeping some whole beans for texture.
Crushing garlic with salt breaks it into a paste that spreads evenly instead of leaving raw chunks.
Keeping some lemon juice for the end preserves its fresh flavour, which fades with long simmering.
variations: Top each bowl with a chopped hard-boiled egg, boiled for 10 minutes until the yolk is firm.
Stir 2 tbsp tahini in with the garlic paste for a richer, nuttier bowl.
storage: Refrigerate the beans without toppings in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat in a saucepan over low heat with a splash of water until hot, stirring often. Add fresh tomato and parsley when serving.

title: Japanese Chicken Soboro Don
summary: Sweet-savoury minced chicken and fluffy scrambled egg served in colourful stripes over rice.

stages.title: Cook the rice
steps: Rinse the rice in a sieve under cold water until the water runs mostly clear, then drain.
Cook the rice according to the packet, using short-grain or sushi rice if you can.
Rest the rice, covered and off the heat, for 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork.

stages.title: Prepare the toppings
steps: Grate the ginger and thinly slice the spring onions.
In a small bowl, mix the soy sauce, mirin and white sugar until the sugar dissolves.
Crack the eggs into a separate bowl, add the salt and beat until no streaks of white remain.

stages.title: Cook the chicken soboro
steps: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Add the chicken mince and ginger, breaking the mince up with a wooden spoon or two spoons as it cooks, for 3–4 minutes until no pink remains.
Pour in the soy mixture and cook over medium heat for 4–5 minutes, stirring constantly, until the liquid has almost evaporated and the mince is fine, glossy and cooked through.
Tip the chicken into a bowl and cover to keep warm.

stages.title: Scramble the eggs
steps: Wipe out the pan and place it over low heat.
Pour in the beaten eggs and stir constantly with a spatula or chopsticks for 3–4 minutes until the eggs form small, soft curds and are cooked through with no liquid egg remaining.
Remove the pan from the heat straight away so the eggs do not turn dry.

stages.title: Assemble the bowls
steps: Divide the rice among four bowls.
Arrange the chicken on one half of each bowl and the egg on the other half.
Scatter the spring onions over the top and serve while warm.

tips: Break the mince up as soon as it hits the pan, before it browns, so it cooks into fine crumbs rather than clumps.
Cooking the eggs over low heat and stirring constantly gives small, tender curds; high heat makes them rubbery.
Simmering the soy mixture until almost dry makes the chicken glossy and seasoned rather than soupy, so it doesn't make the rice wet.
variations: Add blanched green beans or snow peas, sliced thinly, as a third topping for colour and crunch.
Use pork mince instead of chicken and cook until no pink remains.
storage: Store the rice, chicken and egg in separate airtight containers in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat the chicken and rice in the microwave until steaming hot, and the egg until warmed through.

title: French Madeleines
summary: Delicate shell-shaped sponge cakes with buttery edges, lemon zest and a soft centre.
ingredients: 110 g butter, plus 1 tbsp extra, softened, for greasing
1 tbsp plain flour, extra, for dusting the tin

stages.title: Melt the butter and mix the dry ingredients
steps: Melt the 110 g butter in a small saucepan over low heat for 2–3 minutes until completely liquid, then pour into a bowl and leave to cool to lukewarm.
Sift the 120 g plain flour and the baking powder into a medium bowl.
Finely grate the zest of the lemon and set aside.

stages.title: Make the batter
steps: Whisk the eggs and caster sugar in a large bowl with electric beaters on high speed for 5–6 minutes, until pale, thick and doubled in volume.
Whisk in the vanilla extract and lemon zest.
Gently fold in the sifted flour mixture in two batches with a spatula until just combined.
Fold in the cooled melted butter until the batter is smooth and glossy, with no streaks of butter.

stages.title: Chill the batter
steps: Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 45 minutes, until the batter is firm enough to hold its shape when spooned.
Meanwhile, brush the madeleine tin generously with the softened extra butter, dust with the extra 1 tbsp plain flour, then tap out the excess and chill the tin.

stages.title: Bake the madeleines
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) while the batter finishes chilling.
Spoon the batter into the moulds, filling each about three-quarters full without spreading it out.
Bake on the middle shelf for 9–11 minutes, until risen with a hump, golden at the edges and springy when touched in the centre.

stages.title: Unmould and serve
steps: Rap the tin firmly on the bench and tip the madeleines out onto a wire rack, using a spoon to loosen any that stick.
Cool for 10 minutes, then dust with the icing sugar and serve while still slightly warm.

tips: Chilling the batter makes the cold mixture hit the hot oven and puff quickly, which creates the characteristic hump.
Whisking the eggs and sugar until thick traps air, which gives a light, springy crumb without extra raising agent.
Cooling the melted butter stops it from cooking the eggs or deflating the whisked mixture when folded in.
Greasing and flouring the tin, then chilling it, helps the shell pattern release cleanly.
variations: Swap the lemon zest for orange zest and use half the vanilla for a softer citrus flavour.
Dip the cooled madeleines in melted dark chocolate and let it set on baking paper before serving.
storage: Best eaten the day they are baked. Store cooled madeleines in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days, or freeze for up to 1 month and thaw at room temperature.

title: Greek Gemista Stuffed Tomatoes
summary: Oven-baked tomatoes and peppers filled with herbed rice, pine nuts and sweet onions.

stages.title: Hollow the vegetables
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan).
Slice the tops off the tomatoes and capsicums and keep the tops. Remove the seeds and membranes from the capsicums.
Scoop the flesh out of the tomatoes with a spoon, leaving a shell about 1 cm thick. Chop the pulp roughly and keep it with its juices in a bowl.
Stand the tomato and capsicum shells upright, snugly together, in a baking dish.

stages.title: Cook the filling
steps: Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and pine nuts and cook for 1 minute, stirring, until the pine nuts start to turn golden.
Stir in the rice, the chopped tomato pulp and juices, the salt and the black pepper. Cook for 2–3 minutes, stirring, until the juices start to bubble.
Remove the pan from the heat and stir through the parsley and mint.

stages.title: Fill the vegetables
steps: Spoon the filling into the shells until they are about three-quarters full, so the rice has room to expand.
Put the tops back on the tomatoes and capsicums.
Pour the vegetable stock into the base of the dish around the vegetables.
Drizzle the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil over the tops.

stages.title: Bake covered
steps: Cover the dish tightly with foil.
Bake for 40 minutes, until the vegetables have softened and the rice has absorbed most of the stock.

stages.title: Uncover, brown and rest
steps: Remove the foil and bake for a further 15 minutes, until the tops are browned and the stock in the dish has reduced to a few spoonfuls.
Taste a grain of rice from the centre of one capsicum; it should be tender with no firm centre. If it is still firm, cover with foil and bake for 5 minutes more, then test again.
Rest the dish for 10 minutes before serving, spooning the pan juices over each vegetable.

tips: Fill the shells only three-quarters full, because the rice swells as it cooks and will push the tops off if packed in.
Pack the vegetables tightly in the dish so they hold each other upright and cook in the shared steam.
Frying the rice briefly with the onion and oil before baking coats the grains, which helps them stay separate rather than gluey.
Resting the dish before serving lets the juices settle, and the flavours are better warm than piping hot.
variations: Add 2 tbsp sultanas to the filling with the rice for a sweeter, more traditional taste.
Add 1 potato, cut into wedges, to the dish around the vegetables so it cooks in the stock and tomato juices.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat covered in a 180°C (160°C fan) oven for 15–20 minutes until hot throughout. Also good at room temperature.

title: French Leek and Potato Soup
summary: Smooth, buttery leek and potato soup finished with cream and fresh chives.
ingredients: 3 leeks, white and pale-green parts only
500 g potatoes, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps: Trim the leeks, split them lengthways and rinse well under cold running water, fanning the layers to wash out any grit.
Slice the leeks thinly.
Peel the potatoes and cut them into 2 cm cubes.
Snip the chives finely and set aside for serving.

stages.title: Soften the leeks
steps: Melt the butter in a large heavy-based saucepan over low-medium heat.
Add the leeks and the salt and stir to coat in the butter.
Cover and cook, stirring occasionally, for 10–12 minutes until soft and silky but not browned.

stages.title: Simmer the soup
steps: Add the potatoes and the vegetable stock to the pan and stir.
Increase the heat to medium-high and bring to the boil, then reduce to low-medium and partly cover.
Simmer for 18–20 minutes until the potato breaks apart easily when pressed with a fork.
Remove from the heat and cool for 5 minutes before blending.

stages.title: Blend and finish
steps: Blend the soup with a stick blender until completely smooth, or in batches in a blender with the lid vented.
Return to the pan over low heat and stir in the cream, nutmeg and black pepper.
Warm gently for 2–3 minutes without boiling, then taste and add a little more salt if needed.
Ladle into bowls and scatter with the chives.

tips: Rinse the leeks after slicing if they are very sandy, because grit collects between the layers and ruins the smooth texture.
Cooking the leeks gently with a lid on softens them in their own moisture, which gives a sweet flavour that browning would spoil.
Starchy potatoes such as Sebago or Desiree break down for a naturally creamy soup without needing extra cream.
Add the cream off a boil, since high heat can make it split and look grainy.
variations: For a vichyssoise, cool the blended soup without the hot cream step, stir in the cream once cold and chill for at least 3 hours before serving.
Stir in a handful of baby spinach when blending for a green, slightly earthy soup.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat gently over low heat, stirring, until steaming; don't boil. Freeze without the cream for up to 3 months.

title: Mexican Sopa de Fideo
summary: Toasted vermicelli noodles simmered in a light tomato and garlic broth with lime.

stages.title: Blend the tomato base
steps: Put the tomatoes, onion, garlic and 250 ml of the chicken stock in a blender.
Blend for 1 minute until completely smooth, then set aside.
Break the vermicelli into 4–5 cm lengths with your hands.

stages.title: Toast the noodles
steps: Heat the oil in a large deep saucepan over medium heat.
Add the vermicelli and cook for 3–5 minutes, stirring constantly, until evenly deep golden brown.
Take care not to let any strands turn dark brown, as they taste bitter.

stages.title: Simmer the sauce
steps: Pour the blended tomato mixture into the pan, standing back as it will spit.
Cook over medium heat for 5 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce darkens and thickens slightly.
Add the salt and a generous grind of black pepper.

stages.title: Cook the noodles in the soup
steps: Pour in the remaining 750 ml chicken stock and stir well, scraping up anything stuck to the base.
Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, then reduce to medium-low.
Simmer for 5–7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the noodles are tender and the soup has thickened slightly.
Taste and add more salt or pepper if needed.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Ladle the soup into four bowls while hot.
Scatter over the coriander and serve with the lime wedges for squeezing over.

tips: Toasting the vermicelli until golden gives the soup its nutty, savoury flavour, and the coating of oil helps the strands stay separate.
Simmering the blended tomato before adding the rest of the stock cooks off its raw, acidic taste and deepens the colour.
Serve straight away, because the noodles keep absorbing stock and the soup turns thick and stodgy if left standing.
variations: Stir through 2 cups of shredded cooked chicken with the remaining stock for a heartier lunch.
Add 1 tsp chilli flakes with the tomato mixture for a spicier soup.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days. The noodles will absorb the liquid, so add a splash of water or stock when reheating in a saucepan over medium heat until steaming hot throughout.

title: Italian Caprese Stuffed Peppers
summary: Sweet roasted peppers filled with mozzarella, cherry tomatoes and basil, finished with balsamic glaze.
ingredients: 4 capsicums, halved lengthways through the stem, seeds removed
250 g mozzarella, drained and torn into small pieces
1 bunch basil, leaves picked, larger leaves torn

stages.title: Prepare the capsicums and oven
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and line a large baking tray with baking paper.
Halve the capsicums lengthways through the stems and scrape out the seeds and white membranes, keeping the stems on so the halves hold their shape.
Place the capsicums cut side up on the tray, brush the insides and edges with half the olive oil and season with half the salt.

stages.title: Roast the capsicums
steps: Roast the capsicums on the middle shelf for 20 minutes, until the edges are starting to colour and the flesh has softened slightly.
Remove the tray from the oven and leave the oven on at 200°C (180°C fan) for the second bake.

stages.title: Make the tomato filling
steps: While the capsicums roast, combine the cherry tomatoes, garlic, the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, the remaining salt and a good grind of black pepper in a bowl.
Stir through half the basil leaves.
Tip any liquid out of the roasted capsicum halves if it has pooled, then spoon the tomato mixture into them.

stages.title: Bake with the mozzarella
steps: Scatter the torn mozzarella over the tomato filling.
Return the tray to the oven and bake for 10–12 minutes, until the cheese has melted and is lightly golden in spots and the capsicums are tender when pierced with a knife.
Meanwhile, simmer the balsamic vinegar in a small saucepan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes, until syrupy and able to coat the back of a spoon.
Let the capsicums stand for 3 minutes, then drizzle with the balsamic syrup and top with the remaining basil.

tips: Drain the mozzarella and pat it dry with paper towel, because excess whey turns the filling watery in the oven.
Pre-roasting the capsicums for 20 minutes means they are tender by the time the cheese has melted, instead of staying firm.
Keeping the stems on helps the halves sit level and stops the juices running out.
Adding half the basil after baking keeps its fresh flavour and bright green colour; it turns dark and dull if baked.
variations: Spoon 1 cup cooked quinoa into each capsicum half beneath the tomato filling to make it a more substantial meal.
Swap the mozzarella for torn bocconcini or add a spoonful of basil pesto over the tomatoes before the cheese.
storage: Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat in a 180°C (160°C fan) oven for 10–15 minutes until hot through. Not suitable for freezing.
